metadata.title: Software Engineering Mastery — Python-first
metadata.subtitle: Build-first levelled skill tree for backend, CS, DSA, system design, production and later AI
metadata.audience: Developer returning to engineering after approximately two years, prior Node.js experience, Python familiarity through DSA
metadata.target_outcome: Competitive software engineering skill and demonstrable portfolio; no guarantee of ₹40+ LPA compensation or job placement
metadata.content_license: Learner-specific synthesized roadmap; links point to third-party resources that retain their own licenses
metadata.audience_ui: Solo progress tracker; low maintenance, human-friendly, responsive

learner_starting_profile.python: Comfortable with Python syntax and solving DSA exercises, not experienced building full Python backend products
learner_starting_profile.javascript_nodejs: Built projects in Node.js in past, much forgotten after two-year gap; Python chosen intentionally, not because JavaScript is obsolete
learner_starting_profile.near_term_strategy: Python and backend fundamentals, DSA, SQL, practical project and deployment. Later extend to AI/agents after building reliable software.
learner_starting_profile.available_time_assumption: ~5 hours/day, six days/week as an adjustable planning baseline

principles: Build → understand → break → measure → improve; theory first when safety/correctness requires it
Mastery means explanation, independent implementation, testing and trade-off analysis
Introduce frameworks in response to actual pain or requirements, not technology fashion
Progress depends on evidence not chapter completion or calendar time
Debugging, documentation, secure defaults and communication happen throughout
Do not equate a synthetic load test with enterprise production experience
AI specialization builds on APIs, data, security, eval and reliability; postpone advanced agents as requested

L1.label: Foundation
L1.meaning: Explain core principles and independently build small correct examples with reference documentation
L1.gate: Working small implementation, tests, explanation and an unfamiliar variation

L2.label: Professional
L2.meaning: Build and maintain complete reliable systems; diagnose failures and justify designs
L2.gate: Tested feature or app, failure analysis, quality checks, measured changes and explanation

L3.label: Advanced
L3.meaning: Design, optimize and operate more complex systems under explicit workload, reliability and cost constraints
L3.gate: Documented assumptions, experiments, design comparisons, failure recovery and limitations

special_notes.AI_taxonomy: AI includes symbolic search/planning and ML. Generative AI and tool-using agentic workflows overlap but are not a strict nested hierarchy.
special_notes.python_concurrency: Default CPython GIL assumptions depend on build/version; optional free-threaded Python builds exist.
special_notes.source_usage: Official docs for evolving APIs and current behavior; university materials for deep theory; books for long-lived principles.
special_notes.cloud_infrastructure: Kafka and Kubernetes are optional specialized tools, not prerequisites for small reliable products.
special_notes.job_target: Offer levels and salary depend on experience, company and market; the roadmap does not promise a job by a date.
